name: Vengorach
body:
Vengorach
CR 18

This limbless, indigo wyrm has two fire-breathing heads and two poison-dripping tails.

XP 153,600
CE Gargantuan dragon
Init +4; Senses darkvision 60 ft., low-light vision, scent; Perception +31

DEFENSE

AC 34, touch 6, flat-footed 34 (+28 natural, –4 size)
hp 325 (21d12+189)
Fort +21, Ref +12, Will +13
DR 15/magic; Immune fire, paralysis, poison, sleep; Resist acid 10; SR 29

OFFENSE

Speed 20 ft., fly 120 ft. (poor)
Melee 2 bites +32 (4d6+14/19-20), 2 stings +32 (2d6+14 plus poison)
Space 20 ft.; Reach 20 ft.
Special Attacks breath weapon (50-ft. cone, 12d6 fire damage, Reflex DC 29 half, usable every 1d4 rounds)

STATISTICS

Str 38, Dex 10, Con 29, Int 11, Wis 12, Cha 13
Base Atk +21; CMB +39; CMD 49
Feats Alertness, Hover, Flyby Attack, Improved Initiative, Vital Strike, Improved Vital Strike, Greater Vital Strike, Improved Critical (bite), Power Attack, Weapon Focus (bite, sting)
Skills Appraise +24, Fly +14, Intimidate +25, Perception +31, Sense Motive +27, Stealth +12; Racial Modifiers +4 Perception
Languages Draconic

SPECIAL ABILITIES

Breath Weapon (Su)

Each of vengorach’s heads can breathe fire separately. If their areas overlap, a creature caught in that overlapping area takes a -2 penalty on its Reflex saves. Damage done by both breath weapons stacks and is considered to be a single source of fire damage for the purpose of fire resistance. Regardless of how many heads breathe fire, a vengorach can use its breath weapon once every 1d4 rounds.

Poison (Ex)

Sting—injury; save Fort DC 29; frequency 1/round for 6 rounds; effect 1d8 Con; cure 2 consecutive saves. The save DC is Constitution-based.

Synchronized Strike (Ex)

Once per round, a vengorach can perform two bite attacks as an attack action, such as when performing a charge or making an attack or opportunity. When a vengorach uses both bite attacks against a creature that is at least one size category smaller than itself, the attacks are resolved as if both heads were flanking the target.

ECOLOGY

Environment temperate or warm hills
Organization solitary
Treasure standard

Vengorachs are frightening, draconic menaces – that much is known. What is unclear is their lineage, which baffles learned men seeking explanation. Sometimes called emperor wyverns, they clearly have much in common with these lesser dragons, chief among these similarities being the tail tipped with a poisonous stinger, bifurcated as observed in some dangerous wyvern subspecies. Some scholars argue that vengorachs spawned from unions between these vile creatures and true dragons, which others discount as improbable, citing their strange bicranial appearance. Another theory proposes gorynyches and even elder wyrms as potential wyvern mates that could result in vengorachs, but even putting aside the obvious unlikeliness of such a match, size and physical power of these two-headed creatures is vast compared to gorynyches and miniscule compared to elder wyrms.

Scholarly debates matter little to common folk, to whom a vengorach is far more menacing than interesting. Smarter than wyverns, but with a crude and unrefined intellect unlike that of true dragons, vengorachs concern themselves only with worldly pleasures. They are incredibly long-lived, reaching their monstrous sizes far more rapidly than most dragons, but also tend to sleep in hibernation for dozens or reportedly even hundreds of years. When they wake, they spend much time sating their thirst for worldly pleasures. They devour animals, force themselves upon smaller dragons and wreak havoc upon civilized races for simple amusement. That cycle continues for months or years, at which point a satisfied vengorach retreats to its cave to slumber once more.

Heads of a vengorach have no separate minds and they tend to speak with nearperfect synchronicity, but in combat become extremely precise and versatile weapons, able to both breathe fire and bite at different targets and angles, putting pressure on even best-defending opponents and allowing them to deal monstrous damage within a small amount of time. Both heads can breathe fire separately, though they share a reservoir, which lowers the density of the expelled flame.

Vengorachs have no limbs, except for their wings. They prefer flying to other forms of movement and can easily spend most of their waking hours in the air, despite their bulk and relative gracelessness. They do most of their destruction without touching the ground, often thoroughly scorching the area with their powerful flames before lowering to hover and feast on the corpses. When combatting land adversaries impervious to their fire, vengorachs prefer to repeat flyby attacks, both of their heads biting their victims in incredible unison. When forced to land, vengorachs slither across the ground in an ungainly fashion, supporting themselves with dragging motions of their powerful wings.

Vengorachs have much less care for treasure than most dragons, their hoards including only the items that happen to interest them the most. Their mountainous caverns may include only misshapen lumps of various metals fused by flame for easier transportation and a few interesting but damaged statues, much to the chagrin of dragonslayers hoping for treasure troves of gold, gems and magic.
